U1-S1.title: Thinking Like a Physicist

assessment_plan_authority.learning_target: Students will explain how physics uses observation, measurement, evidence, models, and testable claims to understand the natural world.
i_can: I can distinguish between an observation, inference, hypothesis, law, and theory.
I can explain why a claim must be testable to be scientific.
I can use evidence from a short scenario to decide whether a physics explanation is supported and explain why formulas in physics are guides for thinking, not just tools for calculation.
assessment_plan_authority.vocabulary: observation, inference, hypothesis, scientific law, scientific theory, evidence, model, testable claim
assessment_plan_authority.representations: observations and measurements; claim-evidence-reasoning notes; simple model or formula representations
assessment_plan_authority.misconceptions: Treating an inference as an observation; assuming an explanation is scientific because it sounds plausible; treating a formula as a rule with no physical meaning
assessment_plan_authority.applications: Evaluate short physical scenarios, measurements, and competing explanations; connect a simple relationship to the quantities it represents
assessment_plan_authority.recurring_practices: observation and evidence use; model interpretation; scientific explanation

Given two short explanations of the same observation, decide which is better supported and state the missing evidence in the weaker one.
